drafts.content: The routing module predicts boundaries by measuring the cosine similarity between adjacent encoder‑output vectors: it first projects each output \(\hat{x}_t\) to queries \(q_t\) and keys \(k_t\), then computes a boundary probability \(p_t = \tfrac12\bigl(1 - \frac{q_t^\top k_{t-1}}{\|q_t\|\|k_{t-1}\|}\bigr)\) which lies in \([0,1]\) [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. A hard boundary indicator \(b_t\) is set to 1 whenever \(p_t \ge 0.5\), otherwise 0, with \(p_1\) defined as 1.0 to start the sequence with a boundary [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. Lower cosine similarity (i.e., larger \(p_t\)) signals a contextual or semantic shift, prompting the module to place a chunk boundary at that position [HNET:2.2.1:c023].

The routing module computes cosine similarity between adjacent encoder outputs by projecting each \(\hat{x}_t\) to a query \(q_t\) and a key \(k_t\) and then calculating a boundary probability \(p_t = \tfrac12\!\left(1 - \frac{q_t^\top k_{t-1}}{\|q_t\|\|k_{t-1}\|}\right) \in [0,1]\) [HNET:2.2.1:c023]. It then forms a hard boundary indicator \(b_t = \mathds{1}_{\{p_t \ge 0.5\}}\) with \(p_1\) defined as 1.0 to ensure the sequence begins with a boundary [HNET:2.2.1:c023].
